chift_routes.chift_name: Get invoices by type (sale/purchase entries - Multiple Analytic Plans)
chift_routes.one_line: Horus has no general invoice list (invoices.sales.outstanding.list covers only open sales items, without lines), so the connector rebuilds each invoice from the ledger. Headers come from POST /book-entries.list, one call per daybook of BOTH sibling types (200+250 for customer_*, 100+150 for supplier_*), because credit notes may sit in invoice daybooks (D1); the partner is sideloaded. Lines, VAT, analytics, matching and the partner-line sign come from one POST /account-histories.list call. Each entry is classified as invoice or credit note by its daybook type, with the partner-line sign used only in folders without a credit-note daybook (D1, A pending H2); TransactionType on open sales items is only a consistency check. Payments come from a second account-histories.list call joined on MatchNo. tax_code is the connector's synthetic VAT id (D2), reference/customer_memo are split from the header comment (D3), and amounts are in EUR unless invoice-currency totals are known (D4). Pagination, day-level dates, payment_status and approval_status are emulated.

summary: Horus has no general endpoint that lists or reads sales or purchase invoices. The 72-endpoint reference only offers invoices.*.new/update and invoices.sales.outstanding.list/info, which return open sales items only, and pushed invoices 'are converted into book entries in the corresponding daybook' (Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices), so each Chift invoice must be rebuilt from the ledger. The connector caches every daybook (daybooks.list) and, per D1, ALWAYS reads both sibling daybook types (customer_* → 200 Sale + 250 SaleCreditNote; supplier_* → 100 Purchase + 150 PurchaseCreditNote), one book-entries.list call per daybook because DaybookId is singular and required, with the partner sideloaded through Include 'CompanyDetail.Company'. One account-histories.list call returns all lines, VAT, analytics, the partner ledger account, due dates and matching state, grouped by BookEntry.Id. Every entry is then classified by its daybook type (proposed rule: 250/150 = credit note, 200/100 = invoice). Only in a folder without a credit-note daybook, where the create route posts refunds into 200/100, does the partner-line sign decide (customer: net credit = credit note; supplier: net debit = credit note). For sales, TransactionType from invoices.sales.outstanding.list (loaded once per sales request) is a consistency check on open items and never reclassifies. The rule is a heuristic labelled A until Horus answers H2 (document Type on read); Chift chooses between it and a sign-first rule (C5). Payments come from a second account-histories.list call on the partner ledger accounts across all daybooks, joined on (company, account type, MatchNo); payments[].journal_type follows the shared daybook table (D6). Harmonised conventions: lines[].tax_code is the canonical synthetic VAT id (D2), encoded against the folder's tax-combination list (Legislation BE or LU, and direction) and returned only when exactly one entry matches, otherwise null; reference and customer_memo come from splitting the header comment on the first ' | ' (D3, read location A); amounts are treated as folder-currency EUR and a foreign-currency invoice is returned in its own currency only when the open-sales list gives TotalCurrencyAmount, otherwise in EUR with currency 'EUR' (D4); the partner uses the shared company mapper (D9); analytics come from the shared per-folder cache with Free schemas omitted (D8); folder_id follows D7 (a folder not selected at activation is rejected) and every Id-only call checks Data.Folder.Id (D13). Pagination, day-level dates, payment_status and approval_status are emulated because Horus documents no pagination and periods are whole months. The main risks: every update creates a new book entry Id and deletions leave no signal (a periodic full re-sync is proposed), updated_after narrows results only inside the mandatory month window, the invoice/credit-note split is a heuristic pending H2, lines have no quantity or unit price, per-line tax_amount, tax_code identity (null when TaxKind is ambiguous) and payment allocation are approximations, foreign-currency amounts depend on an unconfirmed assumption, and 'paid' is inferred from full matching. GET /book-entries.info reads one entry by Id without a daybook or period, but returns only the header (lines as references, no sideloading), so it serves single-invoice reads and the attachments Document lookup, not the list path. Call budget per request (cold reference cache excluded): one book-entries.list per selected daybook of the two sibling types, one account-histories.list for lines (plus one for payments when requested), and one invoices.sales.outstanding.list for sales types; optional ibans.list per partner.
verdict_rationale: Under the D11 calibration the route is 'supported with workaround'. It is feasible because every core element can be read: header, partner, accounts, VAT rate, analytics, matching and the document reference. It still needs several calls per request: with D = the number of daybooks of the two sibling types (D1), sales need D + 2 (headers, lines, and the open-sales list for the D1 consistency check, D3 and D4) and D + 3 with payments; purchases need D + 1 and D + 2 with payments. An incremental call adds one single-entry call per changed entry that comes back incomplete. A cold cache adds reference calls (folders.info, daybooks.list, fiscal-years.list when dates are missing, accounts.list for the D9 partner account_number, cost-schemas.list plus cost-sections.list per List schema for D8, folders.list only under the D7 fallback). It also needs emulated filters (pagination, day-level dates, payment_status, approval_status) and the D1 invoice/refund split (daybook type, plus a sign heuristic in folders without a credit-note daybook; conditional on H2), and it accepts lost or approximated fields: quantity/unit_price/unit_of_measure, delivery_date, payment_term_id, payment_method_id, withholding_tax, cash-discount terms, Free-schema analytics (D8), partner is_company (always true, D9) and the 'cancelled' status are lost, while per-line tax_amount, tax_code (null when ambiguous, D2), foreign-currency amounts (EUR fallback, D4), payment dedicated_amount and 'paid' (inferred from full matching) are approximations. It is not 'supported' because no native invoice read exists, and not 'not_supported' because all core data is readable.

horus_endpoints.role: Called WITHOUT a Types filter and cached in full per folder. The connector selects the daybooks of BOTH sibling types client-side (D1): customer_invoice / customer_refund → Types 200 + 250; supplier_invoice / supplier_refund → Types 100 + 150. It validates journal_ids against that pair (an unknown id triggers one cache refresh) and builds a map keyed by Id and by SearchKey. Payment lines only carry DaybookSearchKey, so this map resolves payments[].journal_id, journal_name (Heading) and journal_type (Type, through the shared D6 table) for any daybook type.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: cached reference data (1 per folder, per TTL)
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /daybooks.list → Filter.Types (optional): '`100`: Purchase - `150`: PurchaseCreditNote - `200`: Sale - `250`: SaleCreditNote - `500`: Bank ...'; Data[] → Id, SearchKey, Heading, Type, IsUsed; Guide: Data model: 'search key ( SearchKey ), unique within the folder'; Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices: 'types 200 / 250 for sales and 100 / 150 for purchases'

horus_endpoints.role: Invoice header (the anchor object): Id, DocumentNo, Date, Confirmed, Verified, EntryType, LastModifiedDate, CompanyDetail (Company, DueDate, PaymentDate, TotalAmount, TurnoverAmount, TaxAmount, RemarkPayment, RemarkCompany, DiscountDetail), Daybook, Document and AccountHistories refs. Called for every daybook of both sibling types (D1), because a credit note may sit in a 200/100 daybook and an invoice in a 250/150 one. RemarkCompany is the second source of the header comment (D3). CompanyDetail amounts are taken as folder-currency EUR (D4, A). Supports Include sideloading of CompanyDetail.Company. The per-daybook calls can run in parallel.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per daybook of the two sibling types (200+250 or 100+150, after journal_ids) per Chift request (DaybookId is required and singular; D1)
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /book-entries.list: 'Get a list of book entries by folder and daybook, for a given period.' DaybookId *: string; StartMonth *, StartYear *, EndMonth *, EndYear *

horus_endpoints.role: One book entry by Id, with no DaybookId or month window. The response has the same fields as a book-entries.list item: Id, DocumentNo, Confirmed, Verified, EntryType, OperationType, Date, LastModifiedDate, CompanyDetail (Company ref, totals, DueDate, remarks, DiscountDetail), Folder, Daybook, Document and AccountHistories refs. Used (a) to resolve BookEntry.Id → Document.Id for the follow-up attachments route, and (b) as the header call of a single-invoice read or refresh, where Date sets the month window of the account-histories.list Filter.BookEntryId call and Daybook.Id gives the invoice type through the cached daybook map. Not used in the list path: calling it per entry after book-entries.list adds no field (N+1 with no gain). It returns no lines, VAT, currency or matching (AccountHistories are {Type, Id} refs only), and sideloading is not supported on it, so the partner needs companies.info or the cached companies.list. Cross-folder guard (D13): the connector compares Data.Folder.Id with the request's folder_id and returns 400 when they differ, because the call takes only an Id.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 0 in the list path; 1 per invoice on demand (single-invoice read or attachments route)
horus_endpoints.evidence: GET /book-entries.info: 'Get details for a specific book entry.' param[query] Id *: string; Data.Document: object|null {Type: 'Documents', Id}; Data.AccountHistories: array[object] {Type: 'AccountHistories', Id}; Guide: Reading accounting data: 'Use book-entries.info to get the full detail of one entry.'; Guide: Sideloading: 'Sideloading is currently supported on:' book-entries.list, account-histories.list, companies.list, invoices.sales.outstanding.list; GET /book-entries.info → Data.Folder: object {Type: 'Folders', Id}

horus_endpoints.role: Call 1 (all daybooks of both sibling types via DaybookIds, D1): all lines of the candidate entries. Partner lines (AccountType 100/200) give the net debit/credit sign (used by D1 only in folders without a credit-note daybook), CurrencyCode (foreign-currency detection, D4), the partner ledger account, DueDate, MatchNo/MatchStatus and the partner-line Comment (first source of the header comment, D3). Other non-VAT lines give the Chift lines, VAT lines (400) the tax amounts, VatDetail the rate and the components of the synthetic tax_code (D2), CostDetail the analytics (D8). In an incremental call it takes the same ModifiedAfter as the header calls. Call 2 (payments, only when include_payments=true): lines on the partner ledger accounts (Filter.AccountSearchKeys) across ALL daybooks over a wider window, joined on (Company.Id, AccountType, MatchNo).
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per Chift request for invoice lines; +1 when include_payments=true; in an incremental call, plus one single-entry call per changed entry that came back incomplete
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /account-histories.list → Filter.DaybookIds: 'Filters on daybooks specified by their id.'; Filter.AccountSearchKeys: 'Filters on account searchkeys matching the *starts with* clause.'; Guide: Reading accounting data: 'returns every entry line of the folder over a period, across all daybooks'; Filter.ModifiedAfter: '*NULL* by default. Include only account-histories modified after a given date.'; Filter.CompanyId: string // 'Filters on a company specified by its id.'

horus_endpoints.role: Variant with Filter.BookEntryId: all lines of ONE book entry (with VatDetail, CostDetail, MatchDetail and the Document ref) in one call. It is the line call of a single-invoice read or refresh, made after GET /book-entries.info. The month window is still mandatory, so it is set from the book-entries.info Date (that month, optionally widened by 1 month on each side because the period basis is unconfirmed, A). The attachments route no longer needs this call, because book-entries.info returns the Document ref without a period. The daybook type classifies the entry (D1); the partner-line sign is used only in folders without a credit-note daybook.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per invoice, only for a single-invoice read or refresh (never in the list path)
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /account-histories.list → Filter.BookEntryId: 'Filters on a book entry specified by its id.'; StartMonth *, StartYear *, EndMonth *, EndYear *; Data[].Document: object|null {Type: 'Documents', Id}; GET /book-entries.info → Data.Date: string(date-time)

horus_endpoints.role: Sales types only, loaded once per request (cached per folder briefly) and joined on BookEntry.Id. TransactionType ('0: Sale invoice' / '1: Sale credit note') is compared with the D1 classification for open sales items and mismatches are logged; it does not reclassify, so a class stays stable once the item is closed. Remark is the third source of the header comment (D3). TotalCurrencyAmount and Currency are the only read-side invoice-currency amounts (D4). OpenAmount, PaymentStatus, PaymentRemark and LinkedElements (payments, credit notes, miscellaneous operations) serve payments and payment_status. There is no date, daybook or ModifiedAfter filter, so each call returns every open item of the folder.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per Chift request for sales types (customer_invoice / customer_refund), whatever include_payments says, because D3 (Remark), D4 (invoice-currency amounts) and the D1 consistency check use it; 0 for purchase types; payload independent of the requested period
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list: 'Get a list of open invoices (and/or linked payments) for a given folder, and eventually filter on company ids.' Filter: CompanyIds, ConfirmedOnly only; Data[] → TransactionType: '`0`: Sale invoice - `1`: Sale credit note - `2`: Payment - `3`: Miscellaneous operation', TotalCurrencyAmount: number|null, Currency: string|null, Remark: string|null, BookEntry: object|null

horus_endpoints.role: Per-invoice version of the outstanding list (linked elements of one open sales invoice). Not used in the list path because it creates an N+1 pattern. In a single sales invoice read it replaces the whole-folder list: one call by BookEntryId gives TransactionType (D1 consistency check), Remark (D3) and TotalCurrencyAmount (D4) for that entry; a 404 or an empty answer means the item is not open, so the D1 rule alone decides.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per invoice (N+1) in the list path, avoid; 1 per single sales invoice read
horus_endpoints.evidence: GET /invoices.sales.outstanding.info: 'Get information about an open sale invoice/credit note, and its eventual linked elements (partial payments, etc.).'

horus_endpoints.role: Purchases: open supplier lines (BookEntry refs, MatchDetail). Not needed in the recommended design, because the partner lines from account-histories.list call 1 already carry MatchDetail. It has no period or daybook filter, so it returns every open supplier item of the folder.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per Chift request if used (whole folder, whatever the date range)
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /suppliers.outstanding: 'Get a supplier's outstanding debts.' Filter: CompanyIds, IncludeVatDetail, UseAlternateHeading only

horus_endpoints.role: Sales: open customer lines (including credit notes and miscellaneous items, plus ReminderLevel). Not needed in the recommended design (partner-line MatchDetail is enough). It has no period or daybook filter.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per Chift request if used (whole folder)
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /customers.outstanding: 'Get a customer's outstanding debts.' Filter: CompanyIds, IncludeVatDetail, UseAlternateHeading only

horus_endpoints.role: Partner details for the shared company → partner mapper (D9): Name, VatNumber, EnterpriseNumber, ContactEmail, ContactPhone, ContactWebsite, Address/Address2/ZipCode/Locality/CountryCode, Language, ExternalReference, CustomerActivitySuspended, concentration accounts and IBAN refs. Fallback when sideloading is not used or when sideloaded Companies objects lack fields. Folder-scoped, so no extra folder check is needed. Supports sideloading itself.

horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /companies.list: 'Get a list of companies for a folder.' (**Sideloading** is supported for this request.)

horus_endpoints.role: Single partner fetch. Fallback only in the list path. In a single-invoice read it is the partner call, because book-entries.info does not support sideloading (the cached companies.list works too). Cross-folder guard (D13): Data.Folder.Id must equal folder_id, otherwise 400.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per distinct partner (N+1) in the list path, avoid; 1 per single-invoice read when the partner is needed

horus_endpoints.role: Partner bank_accounts (Iban, Bic). Only needed if partner.bank_accounts must be filled.

horus_endpoints.role: Alternative source of analytics (CostSection1..8 per account-history line, joined on AccountHistory.Id) if IncludeCostDetail is unavailable or insufficient.

CostSectionType tells List schemas (100) from Free schemas (900); Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1, so their cost lines are omitted from analytic_distribution with a connector warning (D8).

horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /cost-schemas.list → CostSectionType: '`100`: List - expected values are cost sections - `900`: Free'

Inactive sections are still returned on read, because historic invoices may use them (the 422 rejection of inactive sections applies to the write routes only).

horus_endpoints.cardinality: cached reference data (1 per folder)
horus_endpoints.evidence: GET /folders.info → WithAnalytics: boolean; IsVatLiable: boolean; Legislation: string enum["BE", "LU"]

horus_endpoints.role: Supplies the mandatory month window when the Chift request has no date_from/date_to (for example an updated_after-only sync): proposed default from the start of the current fiscal year to the latest EndDate (C11). Call it with Filter.IncludeFuture=true, so entries already posted in a future fiscal year are covered.

horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /fiscal-years.list → StartDate, EndDate; Filter.IncludeFuture: 'boolean // *FALSE* by default'

horus_endpoints.role: File bytes of the invoice's main document. Not called by this route: it serves the follow-up Chift GET /accounting/attachments when status='yes_to_request'. The Document Id is only ever taken from a book entry whose Data.Folder.Id was checked (D13), because documents.download takes only an Id.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per attachment, on demand (other Chift route)
horus_endpoints.evidence: GET /documents.download: 'Download the bytes for a specific document.' RESPONSE 200: 'The file's bytes.'

horus_endpoints.role: Optional diagnostics only: document Remark, Status, and Type (210/220/300/310). It is not part of the D1 classification (daybook type, with the partner-line sign only in folders without a credit-note daybook) nor of the D3 reference rule, and it is not needed for attachments_info. If called, check Data.Folder.Id = folder_id (D13).
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per document (N+1), avoid by default

horus_endpoints.role: Optional bulk version of documents.info: Type (invoice vs credit note) and BookEntry ref of documents created in a window. Could serve as a diagnostic cross-check of the D1 classification or for annex discovery; it is not part of the D1 rule and is not proven to return annexes.

horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /documents.list: 'Get a list of documents by folder, created between dates.' → Type enum, BookEntry: object|null

horus_endpoints.role: Single line detail. Use only for debugging or as a fallback, never in the list path. Resolving the AccountHistories refs of book-entries.info this way would cost one call per line, so single-invoice reads use account-histories.list with Filter.BookEntryId instead.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 1 per line (N+1), avoid
horus_endpoints.evidence: GET /account-histories.info: 'Get details about a specific account history line, i.e. an account record line.'

horus_endpoints.role: Resolves a company's CustomerConcentrationAccount / SupplierConcentrationAccount Id to its SearchKey for partner.account_number in the shared D9 mapper. Needed whenever include_partner_info=true.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: cached reference data (1 per folder), only when include_partner_info=true
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /accounts.list → SearchKey [example='400000'], IntCategory [example='COLLECCUS']

horus_endpoints.role: D7 fallback only: when the request has no folder_id and the connection stores no folder selection, call it with Mode 0 and use the folder if exactly one is returned; otherwise return 400 'folder_id required'.
horus_endpoints.cardinality: 0 in the normal case; 1 per connection (cached) under the D7 fallback
horus_endpoints.evidence: POST /folders.list → Mode *: '`0`: All folders - For the accountant: All folders. - For the entrepreneur: All folders to which she/he has access.'

call_sequence: 0. Chift resolves consumer_id to the Horus license (its own api_url plus an OAuth token valid 1 hour) and sets FolderId by the D7 rule: folder_id when given; if absent, the single folder selected at activation; if no selection is stored, the single folder returned by POST /folders.list {Mode: 0}; otherwise 400 'folder_id required'. A folder_id outside the activation selection → 400 'folder not selected for this connection' before any Horus call (D7). A Horus 403 on any call → Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)', with the Horus Details.

1. [cached per folder] GET /folders.info?Id={FolderId} returns WithAnalytics, IsVatLiable and Legislation (selects the D2 tax-combination list used to encode tax_code); the first two decide whether CostDetail and VatDetail are worth requesting. When lines are returned and WithAnalytics=true, load the shared D8 analytics cache: POST /cost-schemas.list, then POST /cost-sections.list per List-type schema with Filter.IncludeInactive=true. When include_partner_info=true, load POST /accounts.list for the D9 concentration-account SearchKey.

2. [cached per folder] POST /daybooks.list {FolderId} with NO Types filter. Cache every daybook and index it by Id and by SearchKey. Select the daybooks of BOTH sibling types client-side (D1): customer_invoice and customer_refund → Types 200 + 250; supplier_invoice and supplier_refund → Types 100 + 150. Intersect with journal_ids (split on ','), accepting any daybook of the pair; an unknown id triggers one cache refresh, then 400 'journal not found in this folder' (see the journal_ids row). Optionally skip daybooks with IsUsed=false (A: semantics undocumented).

3. [only if date_from/date_to are missing] POST /fiscal-years.list {FolderId, Filter:{IncludeFuture:true}} to derive the mandatory StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear window (the Chift-defined default window, C11; proposal: from the start of the current fiscal year to the latest EndDate; earliest StartDate to latest EndDate only when Chift requires full history).

4. Build the month window: StartMonth/Year from date_from and EndMonth/Year from date_to, optionally widened by 1 month on each side (assumption: the Horus period may refer to AccountingMonth/AccountingYear rather than Date). Convert updated_after to ISO 8601 with '+00:00' (Guide: Making requests) and subtract the overlap margin (proposal: 5 minutes, A).

5. For each selected daybook of the two sibling types, in parallel: POST /book-entries.list {FolderId, DaybookId, StartMonth, StartYear, EndMonth, EndYear, Filter:{ModifiedAfter?: the step-4 value, EntryTypes?: [100]}, Include: 'CompanyDetail.Company' when include_partner_info=true}. Returns the candidate headers plus Included.Companies. Do not call GET /book-entries.info per entry afterwards: its response has the same fields as a book-entries.list item, so it would add N calls and no data.

6. POST /account-histories.list {FolderId, same window, Filter:{DaybookIds:[all selected daybooks of both sibling types], ExcludedEntryTypes: [0,400,600,800,810,850,900,910,1000] when step 5 uses EntryTypes [100], IncludeReport:false, IncludeCompanyDetail:true, IncludeMatchDetail:true, IncludeVatDetail:true, IncludeCostDetail: WithAnalytics}}. When updated_after is set, pass the same ModifiedAfter here, take the union of the changed BookEntry Ids from steps 5 and 6, and complete incomplete entries with single-entry calls (see the updated_after row): account-histories.list Filter.BookEntryId for an entry whose lines do not sum to its TurnoverAmount, GET /book-entries.info (D13 folder check) for changed lines whose header did not come back, so no invoice is half-built. Fallback while H10 is open: reload lines only for the months containing the changed entries' Dates, ±1 month (A). Group the lines by BookEntry.Id. Partner lines (AccountType 100/200) give the net sign, CurrencyCode, AccountSearchKey, DueDate, MatchDetail and Comment. VAT lines (400) give the tax amounts. Every other non-report line becomes a Chift line. Check that the sum of the lines equals the header TurnoverAmount. This call is needed even when include_invoice_lines=false, because payment_status, due dates, currency detection and, in folders without a credit-note daybook, the D1 classification use the partner line.

7. Classify (D1, A) and filter. (a) Sales types only: POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list {FolderId} once per request (cached per folder briefly), joined on BookEntry.Id; it also feeds D3 (Remark), D4 (TotalCurrencyAmount, Currency) and step 8. (b) Each entry (D1): entries of a 250/150 daybook are credit notes and entries of a 200/100 daybook are invoices; in a folder without a 250 (or 150) daybook, entries of the 200 (100) daybook are classified by the partner-line sign (customer: net credit = credit note; supplier: net debit = credit note; no partner line or zero net = invoice). For open sales items, compare TransactionType with the result and log mismatches; never reclassify. (c) Keep only the entries whose class matches invoice_type. Post-filter Date to [date_from, date_to] at day level. Apply approval_status with the same rule as the response field (see query:approval_status).

8. If include_payments=true (payment_status is decided from the step-6 MatchDetail and never triggers this call): (a) sales types: reuse the step-7a invoices.sales.outstanding.list result (OpenAmount, PaymentStatus and LinkedElements per BookEntry.Id). (b) Both sides: POST /account-histories.list {FolderId, window from the invoice window start to the current month, Filter:{AccountSearchKeys:[distinct partner-line AccountSearchKeys from step 6], IncludeCompanyDetail:true, IncludeMatchDetail:true}} with NO daybook filter, so offsets in any daybook (bank, cash, financial, misc, credit notes, external) are found. Drop the invoice entries' own lines, keep lines whose (CompanyDetail.Company.Id, AccountType, MatchNo) equals an invoice partner line, and resolve each DaybookSearchKey through the step-2 map; journal_type follows the shared D6 table. This call returns every line of the shared collective accounts (e.g. 400000/440000) for all partners and all daybooks from the window start to today; Filter.CompanyId takes a single id. Mitigations: a per-folder cache of partner-account lines refreshed with ModifiedAfter, per-partner calls with Filter.CompanyId when few partners are involved, and the LinkedElements of the open-sales list for open sales items. (c) customers.outstanding / suppliers.outstanding are not needed, because step 6 partner lines already carry MatchDetail.

9. Derive status (draft / posted / paid), payments[], due_dates[] (one element per partner line), attachments_info (Document ref: 'yes_to_request' or 'no') and accounting_info. Apply the harmonised conventions: reference / customer_memo from the header comment split on the first ' | ' (D3: partner-line Comment, then RemarkCompany, then sales Remark); lines[].tax_code from VatDetail through the D2 grammar, null unless exactly one entry of the folder's list (Legislation + direction) matches; amounts in EUR with currency 'EUR' unless step 7a gives TotalCurrencyAmount for a foreign-currency open sales item (D4); main_currency_total = the EUR partner-line amount. Then apply the payment_status filter.

10. Partner: map from Included.Companies (step 5) with the shared D9 mapper (active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended, one 'main' address, is_company = true, account_number = concentration account SearchKey via the step-1 accounts.list). Fallback when it is missing or lacks properties: one cached POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{IsCustomer or IsSupplier:true}}. Optional and N+1: POST /ibans.list {CompanyId} per partner for bank_accounts.

11. Sort deterministically (Date, DaybookSearchKey, DocumentNo, Id), compute total after all post-filters, slice page/size (CHIFT_INTERNAL), and cache the full result set briefly so later pages do not re-read Horus (subject to Chift's answer on caching and timeouts); a folder's cache is cleared after any write made through the connector.

12. Errors during the fan-out: on 401, refresh the token once (serialised per connection) and retry; on 403, return Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details (D7); on 500, retry with exponential backoff (reads are idempotent). If a call still fails, fail the whole Chift request and never return a partial invoice set.

13. Later, outside this route: Chift GET /accounting/attachments?type=invoice&document_id={id} → GET /book-entries.info?Id={id} returns Data.Document.Id in one call, with no daybook or month window. Check Data.Folder.Id = folder_id first, otherwise 400 (D13). Document null → no attachment; a 404 most likely means the Id was replaced or deleted (A) → GET /documents.download?Id={DocumentId} → base64.

14. Later, outside this route: single-invoice read or refresh by Id (for example Chift GET /accounting/invoices/multi-analytic-plans/{invoice_id}, which is not part of this assignment). (a) GET /book-entries.info?Id={id} → header, Folder, Daybook.Id, Date, CompanyDetail and Document; check Data.Folder.Id = folder_id, otherwise 400 (D13). (b) POST /account-histories.list {FolderId, StartMonth/StartYear and EndMonth/EndYear = month of Date (optionally ±1 month, A), Filter:{BookEntryId: id, IncludeReport:false, IncludeCompanyDetail:true, IncludeMatchDetail:true, IncludeVatDetail:true, IncludeCostDetail: WithAnalytics}} → lines, currency, partner ledger account, DueDate, MatchDetail and the partner-line sign (used by D1 only in folders without a credit-note daybook). For a 200/250 daybook, GET /invoices.sales.outstanding.info?BookEntryId={id} gives TransactionType (D1 consistency check), Remark (D3) and TotalCurrencyAmount (D4) for an open item. (c) Partner, when needed: GET /companies.info?Id={CompanyDetail.Company.Id} with the same Folder.Id check (D13), because book-entries.info has no sideloading (or the cached companies.list). (d) Payments, when needed: the step-8b call narrowed with Filter.CompanyId and the partner line's AccountSearchKey. Total: 2 calls (3 for a sales entry), up to 5 with partner and payments, and no scan of every invoice daybook over a guessed period.

field_mappings.horus_source: POST /account-histories.list → Comment
field_mappings.rule: Line Comment, assumed to hold the write-side InvoiceLines[].Comment (no source links the two fields); null → ''.
field_mappings.label: A

field_mappings.horus_source: POST /account-histories.list → CostDetail.CostLines[] (Debit/Credit, Costs[]); alt. POST /cost-histories.list → CostSection1..8 per AccountHistory.Id
field_mappings.rule: Requires IncludeCostDetail=true and a folder with costs. Group by CostSchema; within each schema, sum the cost-line amounts per CostSection; percentage = amount / line base × 100, rounded to integers that sum to 100 with the largest-remainder method (the same method as the D8 write-side allocation). Percentages are computed only when the plan's cost lines sum to the line base; a plan that covers less (a non-mandatory schema left empty on some cost lines) is left out with a connector warning and never rescaled to 100% (proposal; H13). Cost lines of Free schemas (CostSectionType 900, from the shared D8 cache) are omitted and a connector warning is logged. [] when there are no cost lines or WithAnalytics=false.
field_mappings.label: A
field_mappings.evidence: POST /account-histories.list → CostDetail: 'Only when 'IncludeCostDetail' is set to true, and folder is with costs.'; Guide: Data model: 'cost histories are the analytical distribution of account history lines'

field_mappings.horus_source: CostDetail.CostLines[].Costs[].CostSchema.Id (validated against the shared D8 cost-schemas.list cache)
field_mappings.rule: D8: analytic_plan = cost schema GUID Id, the same identifier as the connector's Get analytic plans. A Horus cost schema is the Chift analytic plan (up to 8 per folder). Free schemas (CostSectionType 900) are not returned (D8).
field_mappings.label: D
field_mappings.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'a cost schema is an analytical dimension (e.g. DEPARTMENT ). A folder can use up to 8 cost schemas'

field_mappings.horus_source: CostDetail.CostLines[].Costs[].CostSection.Id; when the ref is missing, CostSectionSearchKey → shared D8 cost-sections.list cache (IncludeInactive=true) → Id
field_mappings.rule: D8: analytic_account = cost section GUID Id, the same identifier as the connector's Get analytic accounts. If CostSection is null on a List schema, resolve CostSectionSearchKey through the folder cache built with IncludeInactive=true, so sections made inactive later still resolve on historic invoices. Values of Free schemas (CostSectionType 900) are omitted with a connector warning, never returned as a search key (D8).
field_mappings.label: D
field_mappings.evidence: Guide: Data model: 'a cost section is a value within a schema (e.g. OFFICE )'; POST /cost-schemas.list → '`900`: Free - expected values are free'; POST /cost-sections.list → Filter.IncludeInactive: '*FALSE* by default'

field_mappings.horus_source: CostDetail.CostLines[].Debit / Credit vs line Debit / Credit
field_mappings.rule: Horus stores amounts, so convert them to whole-number percentages (Chift: 'Only whole numbers... must equal 100%'). Use largest-remainder rounding, the cross-route convention of D8; a 33.33 / 33.33 / 33.34 split becomes 33 / 33 / 34. On small lines the split can differ from the one sent: 0.10 sent as 33/33/34 is booked 0.03/0.03/0.04 and reads back as 30/30/40. Ties go to plan order, then account id.
field_mappings.label: D
field_mappings.evidence: POST /account-histories.list → CostLines[]: 'Debit: number|null', 'Credit: number|null [example=1445.09]'; POST /invoices.purchases.new → CostLines[].Amount: 'The sum of all cost lines' amounts must be equal to the corresponding invoice line's base amount.'

A folder_id outside the activation selection → 400 'folder not selected for this connection' before any Horus call. Horus 403 → Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)', with the Horus Details.

For the payment search: from the invoice window start to the current month. For a single-invoice read: the month of the GET /book-entries.info Date, optionally widened by one month.

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: The invoice date window widened by an arbitrary margin, because document creation date is not the invoice date.

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: The same invoice id; the mandatory month window comes from the book-entries.info Date.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

limitations.description: Horus has no general endpoint that lists or reads sales/purchase invoices. The only invoice read endpoints return open sales items (invoices.sales.outstanding.list/info). GET /book-entries.info reads one book entry by Id, but only its header: the same fields as a book-entries.list item, with lines as {Type, Id} references and no sideloading.
limitations.impact: The invoice is rebuilt from book entries and account-history lines, which means more connector logic and more calls than a native invoice read. book-entries.info only makes single-invoice reads and attachment lookups cheaper; it does not shorten the list path.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: No Horus list documents paging parameters or a total count, so lists are expected to return the full result (deduction; size limits unverified, H5).
limitations.impact: Every Chift page re-reads the whole period from Horus unless the connector caches the result between page calls (subject to the Chift question on caching and timeouts). Large folders over long periods give heavy payloads (gzip recommended) and possible timeouts: expected to work for typical folder sizes; behaviour on large folders is unverified (H5).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Incremental calls and the payment lookup still read large volumes: ModifiedAfter narrows results only inside a mandatory month window, and the payment lookup reads whole collective accounts (Filter.CompanyId takes a single id).
limitations.impact: An hourly updated_after sync on a folder with years of entries, or a request with include_payments=true, can return large payloads; Horus documents no size or rate limits (H5). Deletions, replaced ids and possibly payment changes are not seen by incremental sync, so a periodic full re-sync is needed.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Periods are whole months (StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear) and are mandatory. It is unclear whether they apply to the accounting period or to Date.
limitations.impact: The connector must post-filter by day and may need to widen the window; invoices booked in a different period than their date could be missed.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: book-entries.list accepts one DaybookId per call.
limitations.impact: Call count grows with the number of daybooks of both sibling types (D calls per request, parallelisable), because D1 requires scanning 200+250 or 100+150.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Updating an invoice (invoices.*.update, book-entries.*.update) generates a new book entry with a new Id, and the original attachment is deleted.
limitations.impact: An updated_after sync shows the updated invoice as a new item while the old Id silently disappears; consumers must reconcile on journal_id + invoice_number, which works only for entries that have a number (C7).
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: None of the 72 documented endpoints exposes deleted or replaced book entries (no tombstone or deletion filter).
limitations.impact: Deletions and replaced Ids can only be detected with periodic full syncs, or by probing known Ids one at a time with GET /book-entries.info (N+1; whether a replaced or deleted Id returns '404 Not Found' is undocumented).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Webhooks are mentioned ('adding new webhook types' in Guide: Changes & versioning), but no webhook documentation was provided.
limitations.impact: It is unknown whether push notifications for changes or deletions exist; the design assumes polling.

limitations.description: Book entries and account-history lines carry no invoice/credit-note flag, and the docs do not tie the write-side Type (0/1) to a daybook type. The only documented read-side discriminator is TransactionType on invoices.sales.outstanding.list (open sales items only).
limitations.impact: D1 scans both sibling daybook types and classifies each entry by its daybook type; the partner-line sign decides only in folders without a credit-note daybook, and TransactionType on open sales items is a consistency check, so a class does not change once the item is paid. The rule is a heuristic (A) until Horus answers H2: a credit note keyed into a 200/100 daybook of a folder that has a credit-note daybook comes back as an invoice with negative amounts (Chift decision C5). Scanning both types doubles the book-entries.list calls when credit-note daybooks exist.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: Line quantity, unit price, unit of measure, delivery date, payment term, payment method and withholding tax are not exposed on read.
limitations.impact: quantity=1, unit_price=untaxed_amount, all other fields null; the line detail of the original invoice is lost.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Cash-discount terms (CompanyDetail.DiscountDetail: DiscountDate, DiscountAmount, DiscountRate) and the customer reminder level (ReminderLevel on customers.outstanding) are readable but have no Chift invoice field.
limitations.impact: This information is dropped; worth mentioning to clients doing credit control.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: The per-line tax amount is not stored on base lines (VAT is booked on separate VAT account lines), which line types carry VatDetail is undocumented, there is no VAT-code endpoint, and VatDetail has no TaxKind.
limitations.impact: lines[].tax_amount must be allocated or computed, and tax_rate may have to be read from the VAT line. tax_code uses the canonical synthetic grammar (D2), encoded against the folder's tax-combination list (legislation and direction), and is null whenever the VatDetail components match zero or several entries (several purchase codes differing only by TaxKind, or TaxCondition '4 = Article').

limitations.description: Analytics are stored as amounts per cost line (up to 8 schemas), while Chift expects whole-number percentages per plan.
limitations.impact: Rounding loss: percentages are approximations of the stored amounts, and on small lines the read-back can differ from the split sent (0.10 sent as 33/33/34 reads back as 30/30/40). A plan that covers only part of a line is left out with a warning rather than rescaled to 100% (proposal; H13).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: On the purchase side there is no open-invoice endpoint with linked payments. invoices.sales.outstanding.list covers only open sales items, and the docs do not say whether fully paid invoices appear in it.
limitations.impact: Payments and paid status must be rebuilt from MatchNo matching on the partner accounts, using an extra wide-period account-histories.list call. dedicated_amount is approximate in many-to-many matches, and 'paid' means 'fully matched', which includes offsets by credit notes or misc operations.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: invoices.sales.outstanding.list, customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding accept only FolderId plus CompanyIds (and ConfirmedOnly on the sales list): no date, daybook or ModifiedAfter filter.
limitations.impact: Each call returns every open item of the folder, whatever the Chift date range. Cache it per folder, or rely only on the partner-line MatchDetail from account-histories.list.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: The Horus status model is Confirmed / unconfirmed plus matching. There is no cancelled state and no approval workflow; only an optional Verified flag exists.
limitations.impact: status is limited to draft/posted/paid. approval_status is 'unknown' by default, and the approval_status filter follows Chift's convention for filters the target cannot honour, unless Chift accepts Verified as approval.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Documents are only downloadable as raw bytes; annexes cannot be discovered from the book entry.
limitations.impact: attachments_info.status can only be 'yes_to_request' or 'no', and annexes may be missed by the attachments route.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Documents still being processed by Horus (documents.new, Status WaitingConfirmation, BeingProcessed and so on) are not book entries yet.
limitations.impact: Invoices sent to Horus as files but not yet booked do not appear in this route.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: It is unknown whether matching a payment updates the LastModifiedDate of the invoice entry or of its partner line. The ModifiedAfter description on book-entries.list mentions 'account-histories'.
limitations.impact: An updated_after sync may miss payment-status changes (H10); the connector may need a separate open-items refresh, and a periodic full re-sync is proposed.

limitations.description: Sideloading exists only on 4 endpoints, and book-entries.info is not one of them. The documented relationships are companies, daybooks and folders; including AccountHistories or Document is not documented, and the example shows a reduced Companies object.
limitations.impact: Lines cannot be assumed to arrive with headers in one call, so the separate account-histories.list call stays, and sideloaded partners may need a companies.list fallback. A single-invoice read through book-entries.info needs its own companies.info call for the partner.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: For foreign-currency entries, the docs do not say in which currency Debit/Credit and CompanyDetail amounts are expressed, nor the direction of CurrencyRate. D4 assumes folder-currency EUR everywhere; invoice-currency amounts exist on read only as TotalCurrencyAmount / OpenCurrencyAmount on invoices.sales.outstanding.list.
limitations.impact: Foreign-currency purchases and closed sales invoices are returned in EUR with currency = 'EUR' (the original currency is not visible in this route); only open foreign-currency sales invoices are returned in their own currency, with lines scaled by a derived ratio. accounting_info.main_currency_total is the EUR partner-line amount. If the assumption is wrong, amounts are wrong for non-EUR documents.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: The invoice header Comment carries both reference and customer_memo under the D3 convention ('{reference} | {customer_memo}'), and where that Comment surfaces on read is undocumented (partner-line Comment, RemarkCompany or the sales Remark).
limitations.impact: reference and customer_memo are split from the first non-empty candidate (A). Comments typed in Horus Office without the convention land entirely in reference, and a reference containing ' | ' cannot round-trip.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: Free cost schemas (CostSectionType 900) are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8).
limitations.impact: Their cost lines are omitted from analytic_distribution with a connector warning, so the analytic picture of such folders is incomplete.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: The shared partner mapper (D9) returns is_company = true for every partner and ignores beneficiary data, because Horus stores no individual-versus-company flag.
limitations.impact: Private persons and beneficiaries read as companies, and first_name/last_name are always null: disclosed as data loss.
limitations.label: D

edge_cases.case: A credit note (write Type 1) booked in a Sale (200) or Purchase (100) daybook instead of a credit-note daybook (250/150). The docs neither allow nor forbid it.
edge_cases.handling: Heuristic (A), pending H2. Both sibling daybook types are always scanned. In a folder without a 250 (150) daybook, where the create route posts refunds into 200 (100), the entry is classified by the partner-line sign (net credit on the customer line, net debit on the supplier line = credit note) and returned under customer_refund / supplier_refund. In a folder that has a credit-note daybook, the daybook type decides, so such an entry comes back as an invoice with negative amounts (known limitation of the proposed rule, C5).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Unconfirmed entry with DocumentNo 0.
edge_cases.handling: invoice_number = null, status = 'draft', id = GUID. Warn consumers that the number will change once the accountant confirms the entry. Such an entry has no business key: if the accountant edits it before confirming, the consumer cannot find it again through journal_id + invoice_number (Chift question C7).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Invoice updated in Horus between two syncs.
edge_cases.handling: It comes back with a new id; the old id never comes back. Consumers dedupe on journal_id + invoice_number (Guide: 'reconcile on business identifiers such as the daybook and the entry number'), which is possible only when the entry has a number (C7).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: A change is committed around the updated_after boundary, or by a long-running write that commits after the consumer's cut-off.
edge_cases.handling: Pass updated_after minus a small overlap as ModifiedAfter; consumers dedupe by id. Boundary semantics, LastModifiedDate precision and clock are undocumented (H10). A periodic full reconciliation catches what incremental sync misses, including deletions and replaced ids.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Invoice updated via invoices.*.update without resending the file.
edge_cases.handling: The new entry has Document=null, so attachments_info.status='no'. Do not carry the attachment state over from the old Id (Guide: 'the original attachment is deleted in both cases').
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Invoice dated 31 March but booked in the April accounting period (or the reverse).
edge_cases.handling: Widen the month window by plus or minus 1 month and post-filter on Date. Confirm the filter basis with Horus.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Date range spanning several fiscal years, or no date range with updated_after only.
edge_cases.handling: No date range: the default window agreed with Chift (C11; proposal: from the start of the current fiscal year to the latest EndDate). A range over several fiscal years uses the requested bounds. If Horus limits the period span, split the calls per fiscal year (unknown, H5).

edge_cases.case: No date range, and entries already exist in a future fiscal year (for example invoices dated next January).
edge_cases.handling: Call fiscal-years.list with Filter.IncludeFuture=true, because the default is FALSE.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Foreign-currency invoice (CurrencyCode e.g. 'USD', CurrencyRate set).
edge_cases.handling: D4: open sales item with TotalCurrencyAmount on invoices.sales.outstanding.list → currency = Currency, total = TotalCurrencyAmount, other amounts scaled by TotalCurrencyAmount ÷ TotalAmount. Otherwise (purchases, closed sales items) → all amounts in EUR with currency = 'EUR', flagged as a limitation. main_currency_total = EUR partner-line amount. CurrencyRate direction stays an open question.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Invoice with several VAT rates (several base lines plus several VAT lines).
edge_cases.handling: Allocate VAT lines by VatCode/VatRate to the base lines; put the rounding difference on the last line so line taxes add up to the header tax.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Purchase with non-deductible VAT or a PersonalShare split.
edge_cases.handling: Extra general or personal-share lines appear. Map them as additional Chift lines and flag that tax_amount may not equal rate × base.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Entry lines with AccountType 0 (Undefined) or 500 (Cash) inside an invoice entry.
edge_cases.handling: Treat them as Chift lines (not partner or VAT), and run the reconciliation check: sum of lines = header untaxed amount.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Partially paid invoice (MatchStatus 0, sales PaymentStatus 10).
edge_cases.handling: status 'posted'; counted as unpaid for payment_status; payments list the partial payments; the open amount comes from OpenAmount (sales).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Invoice fully offset by a credit note or a miscellaneous operation rather than a payment.
edge_cases.handling: MatchStatus 900, so status = 'paid' and payment_status=paid includes it. The offsetting entry appears in payments[] with journal_type customer_refund/supplier_refund or miscellaneous_operation. Chift must accept that 'paid' means 'fully matched'.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: One bank payment settles several invoices (one MatchNo, many invoices).
edge_cases.handling: The payment appears under each invoice with amount = full payment, and dedicated_amount allocated (FIFO or pro rata).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Payment booked in a later month or fiscal year than the invoice window.
edge_cases.handling: The payment search window runs from the invoice window start to the current month, not to date_to.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Advance payment booked before the invoice window.
edge_cases.handling: It is missed by the payment search unless the window start is moved earlier (for example to the fiscal-year start). Choose a margin with Chift.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Offsetting line booked in a daybook type outside the usual payment set (610, 690, 700, 990, or a sales/purchase daybook).
edge_cases.handling: Covered: the payment call filters on the partner ledger accounts with no daybook whitelist, and journal_type is resolved from the full daybook map.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Entry keyed in Horus Office with several partner lines (instalments) with different DueDates.
edge_cases.handling: due_dates gets one element per partner line; due_date = latest DueDate. Outstanding items return such an entry as one item per partner line, each with its own due date (see that route); both routes rely on the same Horus question (H8).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Analytic split that does not give whole percentages (e.g. 1000 split 333.33/333.33/333.34).
edge_cases.handling: Largest-remainder rounding gives 33/33/34. Document the approximation. On very small amounts the read-back can differ visibly (0.10 → 30/30/40).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: A cost schema covers only part of a line (e.g. line 1,000; cost line 1 DEPARTMENT=OFFICE, PROJECT=P1 for 600; cost line 2 DEPARTMENT=SHOP for 400).
edge_cases.handling: Return DEPARTMENT (100% covered) and leave PROJECT out with a connector warning, rather than inflating P1 to 100% (proposal). Whether Horus allows a cost line without a value for a non-mandatory schema is H13.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Free-value cost schema (CostSectionType 900) with no CostSection Id.
edge_cases.handling: Omitted from analytic_distribution and a connector warning is logged (D8: Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Folder without analytics (WithAnalytics=false) or not VAT liable.
edge_cases.handling: analytic_distribution = []; tax_rate = 0, tax_code = null (VatDetail is only returned for VAT-liable folders).
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Entry without a partner (CompanyDetail null).
edge_cases.handling: partner_id = null, partner = null; totals taken from the lines.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Partner is a beneficiary company (employee or manager, a natural person).
edge_cases.handling: D9: beneficiary flags are ignored (beneficiaries are out of scope). is_company = true, first_name/last_name = null, active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended (A). Disclosed as data loss.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Sideloaded Companies objects come back with fewer fields than companies.list (the guide example shows only Id, SearchKey, Name, Address).
edge_cases.handling: Detect missing properties and fall back to one cached POST /companies.list {FolderId} per folder.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Entry without a document.
edge_cases.handling: attachments_info.status = 'no'.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: journal_ids contains a daybook outside the sibling pair of invoice_type (e.g. a bank daybook for customer_refund).
edge_cases.handling: Per Chift's convention: 400 naming the id, or ignore it and return an empty page if no daybook of the pair remains. A 200 daybook in a customer_refund request is valid (D1). An id that is still unknown after one cache refresh → 400.

edge_cases.case: payment_status=paid for sales invoices that no longer appear in invoices.sales.outstanding.list.
edge_cases.handling: Decide from the partner-line MatchStatus 900 found by account-histories.list, not from the outstanding list.

edge_cases.case: Entries in an invoice daybook with a non-Normal EntryType or OperationType (e.g. Vat, Reclassification).
edge_cases.handling: Optionally restrict to EntryTypes [100] (and ExcludedEntryTypes on the line call). Validate with Horus whether such entries exist in invoice daybooks.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Opening or report lines (IsReport=true).
edge_cases.handling: Exclude them with IncludeReport=false or a post-filter on IsReport.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: 401 or 500 in the middle of the multi-call sequence (access tokens last 1 hour).
edge_cases.handling: On 401, refresh the token once (serialised per connection) and retry. On 500, retry with exponential backoff. If it still fails, fail the whole Chift request; never return a partial result.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Single-invoice read or attachments request for an Id that has since been replaced by an update or deleted.
edge_cases.handling: GET /book-entries.info presumably answers '404: Not Found – the resource was not found' (its behaviour for replaced entries is undocumented). Return a Chift not-found error; the consumer re-syncs and finds the new Id through journal_id + invoice_number, which works only when the entry has a number. An Id that belongs to another folder (Data.Folder.Id ≠ folder_id) returns 400 (D13).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Single-invoice read where the entry is booked in a different accounting month than its Date.
edge_cases.handling: Widen the account-histories.list (Filter.BookEntryId) window by 1 month on each side of the book-entries.info Date; if no lines come back, retry with the fiscal-year bounds. Confirm the period basis with Horus.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Entry in a Sale (200) daybook whose customer line is a net credit (or a Purchase (100) entry whose supplier line is a net debit).
edge_cases.handling: Folder without a 250 (150) daybook: classified as a credit note by the sign (D1) and returned by customer_refund / supplier_refund, although its journal_id points to the 200/100 daybook. Folder with a credit-note daybook: returned as an invoice with negative amounts (daybook first, D1).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Entry with no partner line (CompanyDetail null, no AccountType 100/200 line) or a partner net of zero.
edge_cases.handling: The daybook Type decides: 200/100 = invoice, 250/150 = credit note (D1).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Open sales item whose TransactionType contradicts the D1 classification.
edge_cases.handling: The D1 rule decides; log the mismatch for review. The class does not change when the item is later closed and drops off the open-sales list.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Customer or supplier invoice with a credit-direction total (a negative invoice), which Chift's due-date sign convention allows.
edge_cases.handling: Daybook first (D1): returned under customer_invoice / supplier_invoice with negative amounts. Only in a folder without a credit-note daybook does the sign heuristic return it as a refund (known limitation; Chift decision C5).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Header comment without ' | ' (only a reference was written, or the text was typed in Horus Office).
edge_cases.handling: The whole text becomes reference and customer_memo = null (D3). A comment '| text' gives reference = null and customer_memo = 'text'.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Purchase line whose VatDetail matches several catalogue entries that differ only by TaxKind, or a line with TaxCondition 4 (Article).
edge_cases.handling: tax_code = null; tax_rate and tax_amount are still returned (D2). Never guess the code and never return VatCode (its meaning is undocumented, H1).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Foreign-currency sales invoice that is paid or otherwise closed between two syncs.
edge_cases.handling: It drops off invoices.sales.outstanding.list, so its amounts switch from invoice currency to EUR with currency = 'EUR' (D4). Warn consumers, or let Chift choose a stable EUR representation (open question).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: folder_id missing on a connection with several selected folders.
edge_cases.handling: 400 'folder_id required' (D7).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: folder_id of a folder the Horus user can access but that was not selected at Chift activation.
edge_cases.handling: 400 'folder not selected for this connection' before any Horus call (D7), unless Chift confirms its platform rejects it upstream (C12).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Horus answers 403 (the connected user may not access the folder or perform the action).
edge_cases.handling: Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)', with the Horus Details (D7); no retry.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Historic invoice whose cost line uses a cost section that has since been made inactive.
edge_cases.handling: Returned normally: the D8 cache is built with IncludeInactive=true; the 422 rejection of inactive sections applies only to the write routes.
edge_cases.label: D

No source says what it returns for a replaced or deleted Id beyond the generic '404: Not Found – the resource was not found', and no documented field backs the guide's 'full detail' wording beyond the header.

Resolved: the accepted tax-combination spreadsheets (Tax-combinations-sales.xlsx / -purchases.xlsx) linked from the invoice reference pages were downloaded on 13 Oct 2026 (appendix C) and feed the D2 catalogue per legislation and direction. The list of relationships that can be sideloaded is only given by example (CompanyDetail.Company, Daybook, Folder); no Include property appears in any request schema; the example Included.Companies object shows only 4 properties; the example's endpoint is not named (inferred from its body).
The docs do not state whether a Type 1 credit note may be booked in a 200/100 daybook; the guide only lists 'types 200 / 250 for sales and 100 / 150 for purchases'.
The sign convention of LinkedElements[].TotalAmount comes only from an example value (-210).

Webhooks are mentioned in Guide: Changes & versioning ('adding new webhook types'), but no webhook documentation, Quickstart, Support & FAQ, Changelog or Postman collection was provided.

Currency semantics of Debit/Credit and CompanyDetail amounts for foreign-currency entries and the direction of CurrencyRate are undocumented, and no folder currency field exists; D4 therefore rests on an assumption (A).

No documented way to list the annexes of a book entry (book-entries.documents.annexes.new writes them; no read counterpart, and GET /book-entries.info also exposes only the single Document reference).
Semantics of daybooks.list IsUsed and companies.list CustomerActivitySuspended are undocumented, although the shared partner mapper (D9) uses CustomerActivitySuspended for active.

account-histories.list VatDetail has no TaxKind, and its TaxCondition enum has an extra value '4 = Article' absent from the write enum (0-3), so purchase VAT codes cannot always be rebuilt on read (D2).
No source says where the invoice header Comment (invoices.*.new → Comment) surfaces on read: the partner-line Comment, CompanyDetail.RemarkCompany and the sales Remark all lack a description (D3).

No source documents a read-side invoice/credit-note flag on book entries or account-history lines, or which write-side Type a daybook accepts, so the D1 classification cannot be verified from the docs.
ba_insights: Horus is a ledger: invoices go in through invoices.*.new/update but come back out only as book entries (header) plus account-history lines. To explain it to a client: 'Horus lets you send an invoice, but you read it back as an accounting entry, so we rebuild the invoice from its journal lines.'

Why several calls are needed: each part of a Chift invoice lives in a different Horus resource. Header → book-entries.list (one call per daybook of both sibling types); lines, VAT, analytics, currency, partner account, due dates, matching and the partner-line sign (used by D1 only in folders without a credit-note daybook) → account-histories.list; TransactionType (sales, D1 consistency check), invoice-currency totals and the sales Remark → invoices.sales.outstanding.list; payments → MatchNo matching on the partner accounts; partner → companies (sideloaded) plus accounts.list for the concentration account; attachment → Document ref, downloaded via documents.download. This is the multi-endpoint case the brief warns about.

Terminology to defend: Horus 'folder' = Chift folder (legal entity); Horus 'company' = Chift partner (client, supplier or beneficiary), NOT the legal entity; 'daybook' = journal; 'book entry' = invoice/entry header; 'account history' = ledger line; 'cost schema' = analytic plan; 'cost section' = analytic account; 'cost history' = analytic distribution of a line; 'MatchNo' = matching number. By deduction from the matching rules, MatchNo is allocated per customer, per supplier or per general account, so it is not unique across the folder.

Selecting invoice_type (D1): read both sibling daybook types (200 + 250 for sales, 100 + 150 for purchases). Proposed rule, daybook first: 250/150 = credit note, 200/100 = invoice; the partner-line sign is used only in folders without a credit-note daybook, where the create route's fallback posts refunds into 200/100. TransactionType on open sales items is a consistency check, not an override, so the class is stable over the document's life. Do not use EntryType. The alternative (sign first everywhere) would return every negative invoice as a refund, although Chift's contract allows negative invoices. A until Horus exposes the Type (H2); Chift chooses (C5).

Filter emulation: folder_id and journal_ids (DaybookId/DaybookIds) are native. updated_after maps to ModifiedAfter on book-entries.list and account-histories.list, inside a mandatory month window; whether it reflects matching changes is unconfirmed (H10), and deletions and replaced ids are not reported. date_from/date_to are native only at month level and need a day-level post-filter. page/size, payment_status and approval_status are fully emulated in the connector, so their cost does not shrink with page size.

Prefer bulk calls over N+1. One account-histories.list call with DaybookIds returns all lines of all invoices in the window; grouping by BookEntry.Id replaces one call per invoice. The same applies to payments: one account-histories.list call filtered on the partner ledger accounts (no daybook whitelist, which would miss offsets) joined on (company, account type, MatchNo), instead of invoices.sales.outstanding.info per invoice.

Load all daybooks once, not only the sales or purchase ones. Payment lines only carry DaybookSearchKey, so the connector needs the full daybook list (keyed by SearchKey) to fill payments[].journal_id, journal_name and journal_type.

Call count for a typical request (customer_invoice, folder with 1 Sale and 1 SaleCreditNote daybook, 1 quarter, lines + partner + payments): book-entries.list ×2 with Include=CompanyDetail.Company, account-histories.list ×1 (lines), invoices.sales.outstanding.list ×1 (D1 consistency check, D3 Remark and D4 currency totals; always for sales) and account-histories.list ×1 (payment lines) = 5 calls per request, more with a cold cache (folders.info, daybooks.list, accounts.list, and cost-schemas.list + cost-sections.list per List schema when analytics are on). supplier_invoice with 3 Purchase daybooks and 1 PurchaseCreditNote daybook: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 (no open-items list on the purchase side). General formula, with D = daybooks of both sibling types: sales D + 2 to D + 3, purchases D + 1 to D + 2. The naive N+1 design for 50 invoices is about 1 + 50 (lines) + 50 (companies.info) + 50 (outstanding.info) + 50 (documents.info), roughly 200 calls.

What sideloading changes: Include=CompanyDetail.Company on book-entries.list returns the partners in the same response, so include_partner_info costs zero extra calls instead of N companies.info calls. A cached companies.list (1 call) gives the same result but loads every company in the folder, and it remains the fallback if sideloaded objects are partial. Sideloading only exists on book-entries.list, account-histories.list, companies.list and invoices.sales.outstanding.list (Guide: Sideloading); it does not remove the lines call and does not cover IBANs (ibans.list is still N+1).

Guide: Reading accounting data drives the design. It lists the account-histories.list filters (DaybookIds, CompanyId, NotMatchedOnly, ConfirmedOnly, Include*Detail), says 'Periods are expressed by month and year', recommends ModifiedAfter for incremental sync, and warns 'Updated entries get a new Id ... reconcile on business identifiers such as the daybook and the entry number'. It also points to book-entries.info for 'the full detail of one entry'. That endpoint is documented: it takes only an Id (no daybook or period) and returns the same header as a book-entries.list item, without lines or sideloading. So it changes neither the list path nor its call count, but it makes the attachments lookup a single call and a single-invoice read 2 calls (book-entries.info + account-histories.list with Filter.BookEntryId), 3 for a sales entry (invoices.sales.outstanding.info for the D1 consistency check, D3 and D4), up to 5 with partner and payments.

Status mapping is driven by the Horus workflow, not by payments alone. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default (Guide: Data model) unless the proposed direct posting mode is chosen (C1), so Confirmed=false → draft and Confirmed=true → posted. Full matching (MatchStatus 900) → paid, but this is an assumption: matching also covers credit notes and misc operations. 'cancelled' cannot be produced because Horus replaces or deletes entries instead of cancelling them.

attachments_info is always 'yes_to_request' or 'no': Horus exposes a Document reference on the entry and returns raw bytes through documents.download, never a URL. This matches Chift's base64 GET /accounting/attachments pattern. An invoice update deletes the attachment, so the new entry shows 'no' unless the file is sent again.

Label honesty matters: the verifiers downgraded several claims from F to D or A (tax_rate from VatDetail, line description from Comment, folder currency EUR, 'paid' = fully matched, beneficiary partners as legal entities). When presenting to a client, separate what the docs state from what we infer and from what Horus must confirm.

Why 'workaround' and not 'supported' (D11): everything important is readable, but the connector needs D + 1 to D + 3 calls, several emulated filters (including the D1 split, a heuristic pending H2) and approximations (per-line tax, tax_code that is null when ambiguous, EUR fallback for foreign currencies, whole-number analytic percentages, dedicated_amount, 'paid'), and some fields are lost (quantity/unit price, delivery date, payment term/method, withholding, cash discount, Free-schema analytics, is_company). Recommended next step: put the open questions to Horus (developer@horus-software.be) before build, mainly the credit-note daybook rule, confirmation of the tax-combination files and TaxKind on read, where the header Comment surfaces on read, the currency of amounts and CurrencyRate, the period basis, VatDetail placement, ModifiedAfter semantics and what book-entries.info returns for replaced Ids.

Cross-route consistency is part of the deliverable: the same Horus data must read back the way the create routes wrote it. That is why the read side reuses the shared conventions: one daybook-type table (D6), one synthetic VAT-code grammar (D2: 'S-21-0-0', 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true'), one header-Comment convention (D3: '{reference} | {customer_memo}'), one currency assumption (D4), one partner mapper (D9) and one analytics cache (D8). To a client: 'what you post through Chift comes back identical through Chift, and where Horus cannot carry a value we say so instead of guessing'.

How to explain tax_code to a client (D2): Horus has no VAT-code list; a VAT treatment is a combination of rate, origin, type and (purchases) kind and condition. The connector turns each accepted combination, taken from the Horus tax-combination files for the folder's legislation (BE or LU) and direction, into a stable id. On read, Horus does not return TaxKind, so when two purchase codes differ only by kind the connector returns no code rather than a wrong one; the rate and the amount are always returned.

How to explain currencies (D4): Horus ledger amounts are assumed to be in the folder currency (EUR). Invoice-currency amounts are only visible for open sales invoices, so other foreign-currency invoices come back in EUR, labelled 'EUR', rather than as EUR numbers carrying a USD label. accounting_info.main_currency_total always holds the EUR amount.
